name: Special Pleading
shortDef: Exempting yourself or a favorite from a rule without a relevant reason.
definition: Applying a rule or standard to others while carving out an exception for oneself, one's group or a favored case, without giving a difference that is actually relevant to the purpose of the rule.
howToSpot: Is a rule applied to others but waived for the speaker or a favorite?
What makes this case different, and is that difference relevant to the rule?
Would the speaker accept the same excuse from someone else?
classicExample: Everyone should pay their parking tickets on time. Mine are different, though; I was only running in for a minute.
legitimateVersion: An exception is fair when there's a stated difference that's relevant to the rule's purpose and would apply to anyone in the same spot, like waiving late fees because the payment system was down.

contrast.fal_no_true_scotsman: Special pleading exempts a case from a rule; no true Scotsman redefines a group so a counterexample no longer counts as a member.
contrast.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Special pleading carves out an exception to a standard; moving the goalposts raises the standard after someone has met it.
